doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How Stan Kenton hired him and the Innovations orchestra
summary: Kenton phoned him personally; Kirchner explains his financial loss on the Innovations band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Speaking of the Kenton tour that brings us to the point where you went on the Kenton band. Shall we move into that or is there something else you want to talk about first?
How did you get on the Kenton band?
Yes. I was very pleased and surprised. Apparently, Richie Kamuca was joining the band the same day. He said: “I’m trying for more of a jazz band now.”
He’d lost his shirt on the Innovation band. He lost one hundred and twenty five thousand dollars in four months with that forty-piece band with strings and French horns.
Yeah, and a lot of other people. Shorty Rogers . . .
Yeah. All those guys wrote charts but apparently he lost his shirt on it. It was just too big of a band to support even if the music was popular.
I think he got kind of a rough deal. He was trying to cover a lot of ground but he was really interested in playing some good music and he was also interested in paying for the salaries.
He put his money where his mouth was.
